moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Two-phase fight. Integral Test torches the absolute, but AST grabs control. Conditional convergence. You didn't flinch.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: You crushed the unarmored form and walked away—while its alternating second phase stood right up. Never sheath early.

moves.name: Absolute Convergence Check
moves.professor: Good instinct to inspect the unsigned series first. It diverges, so AST is still needed for the final classification.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. No verdict. This enemy needs comparison plus alternating structure.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Same blueprint. Absolute form falls to comparison, but the alternating shell holds. Conditional. Clean execution.

moves.name: Absolute Series Check
moves.professor: Stripped the sign and saw a beast—but called it tame. Absolute diverges; you misread the territory.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Useful for showing the absolute series behaves like ln n/n and diverges, but AST completes the classification.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. The test stalls before the real fight starts.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: e^{-n^2} slides right under e^{-n}. Geometric r=1/e converges. One swift containment.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Also lands. Ratio limit 0. Solid backup.

moves.name: Root Test
moves.professor: Also crushes it: the nth root tends to 0. A clean alternate route.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: No alternating sign pattern is driving this one. Wrong battlefield.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Smaller than p=2. Converges. Effortless parry.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Limit 1, same outcome. Smooth.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Valid, but more work than comparing to a p-series.

moves.name: nth-Term Test
moves.professor: The terms go to zero, so nth-Term Test gives no conclusion.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Strictly larger than half the harmonic. Diverges. No escape.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Limit 1/2. Same grave.

moves.name: Harmonic Series Recognition
moves.professor: It is essentially the odd harmonic series. Same divergent fate.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. Nothing useful from that swing.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: ln n > 1 soon enough, so terms loom over the shifted harmonic. Diverges. Quick read.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Also does the job.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Works, but comparison sees the divergence faster.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. This test refuses to speak.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: The alternating harmonic in disguise. Conditional convergence—the old faithful.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Absolute is harmonic. Diverges. You bit on the shiny surface.

moves.name: Absolute Series Check
moves.professor: Correct supporting move: the absolute series diverges like harmonic, so the convergence is conditional.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. No help against the alternating harmonic.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Factorial detonates. Ratio sends radius to 0. Only {0} survives. Decisive.

moves.name: Geometric Series Test
moves.professor: Not geometric. You swung at an illusion.

moves.name: Root Test
moves.professor: Also detects the factorial explosion and forces radius 0.

moves.name: Endpoint Check
moves.professor: Endpoints cannot rescue a radius that has already collapsed to 0.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio crunches it. Limit zero. Converges. Sharp.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Monotonic check's messy. Ratio is the clean weapon here—why wrestle?

moves.name: Root Test
moves.professor: It can show convergence, but Ratio Test handles the product structure more directly.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: The product denominator needs a sharper tool than a casual comparison.

questions.question: Find the sum of the series.

moves.name: Known Series Recognition
moves.professor: Arctan engine humming. √3 π/6. Instinct recognition.

moves.name: Numerical Approximation
moves.professor: Decimal approximates, but the boss demands exact. Wrong mode.

moves.name: Power Series Integration
moves.professor: You can derive the arctan series from integration, but recognition is faster.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: It only says convergence. The question asks for the sum.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Limit 1. Total blackout. Knowing a dud weapon saves the fight. Sharp instinct.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Works, but the question asked for the dud. Right blade, wrong target.

moves.name: nth-Term Test
moves.professor: The terms tend to zero, so this test is also inconclusive, but Ratio is the clean named dud here.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Valid for divergence, but not the inconclusive test the question asks for.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Log-log trap snapped. Diverges. Clean execution of the Integral Test.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Smaller than harmonic, can't conclude. Your blade met air.

moves.name: Harmonic Comparison
moves.professor: ln n isn't enough armor. Still divergent. Gut instinct betrayed you.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Can confirm the logarithmic harmonic behavior, though the integral route is clearer.

moves.name: Known Series Recognition
moves.professor: That's cosine in armor. Everywhere. (-∞,∞). Vision like that wins battles.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Also yields ∞. Works, just slower to see.

moves.name: Root Test
moves.professor: Also gives infinite radius. Recognition just sees the whole picture instantly.

moves.name: Endpoint Check
moves.professor: There are no finite endpoints to check when the radius is infinite.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Term ~ 1/n^2. Converges. Spotted the small-angle echo. Dead on.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Way smaller. You'd call divergence on a phantom. Costly.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Valid, but the local estimate ln(1+1/n) ~ 1/n is much quicker.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. It cannot separate convergence from divergence here.

moves.name: Geometric Series Test
moves.professor: Shifted geometric series with ratio (x-3)/3. Radius 3. Sniper precision.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Gets there. Just a step slower.

moves.name: Endpoint Check
moves.professor: Useful after finding the radius: the endpoints are 0 and 6.

moves.name: Taylor Series Formula
moves.professor: No need for derivatives. This is already a geometric series.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: AST holds firm, absolute crumbles. Conditional. You read the terrain perfectly.

moves.name: Absolute Series Check
moves.professor: p=1/3 diverges. The alternating coat doesn't make it absolute.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. The alternating structure is the real opening.

moves.name: p-Series Test
moves.professor: Good for the absolute check: p=1/3 diverges, so convergence is conditional.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: p=3/2 > 1. Converges. No sweat.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Heavy but valid.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Compare with 1/n^{3/2}; same convergent behavior.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. It gives no decisive result.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: p=3 swallows ln n whole. Converges. Textbook smother.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Limit 1, no conclusion. Good dodge.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Valid backup, though comparison is faster.

moves.name: nth-Term Test
moves.professor: Terms tending to zero does not prove convergence.

questions.question: Which test quickly handles this series?

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Exponential steamrolls the polynomial power. Diverges. Ratio Test is lightning here.

moves.name: Root Test
moves.professor: Also swift. Different grip, same speed.

moves.name: nth-Term Test
moves.professor: Also enough: the terms do not tend to zero because the exponential wins.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: A simple p-series comparison misses the exponential growth.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Alternating harmonic's lanky cousin. AST works, absolute falls. Conditional convergence. All angles covered.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Absolute mirrors harmonic. Diverges. You missed the trap.

moves.name: Absolute Series Check
moves.professor: Correct supporting move: the absolute series behaves like harmonic and diverges.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio limit is 1. It cannot classify the alternating series.
